paragraphs: Hyman describes him as the father-in-law of Rav Papa and of Rav Papa’s son Abba, both of whom married his daughters, citing Ketubot 39b and 52b and Sanhedrin 14b.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The saved William Davidson paragraphs in Ketubot 39b and 52b concern Rav Papa’s wife and his son’s betrothal in Abba of Sura’s household; Sanhedrin 14b concerns Rav Papa and his father-in-law. They do not independently establish that the son’s name was Abba, which is retained as Hyman’s statement.

The whole Davidson Ketubot 39b paragraph has Rav Papa quoting the daughter of Abba of Sura; Ketubot 52b has him arranging his son’s marriage into that household; Sanhedrin 14b names Rav Papa and the daughter of Abba of Sura. They do not explicitly name the son Abba. Hyman’s family reconstruction and son’s name remain his statements, with the existing qualification verbatim and no new genealogy admission.
